kicker: MLR570 · a visual guide to our survey
title: From gradients to curvature and matrix geometry: optimization methods for deep networks
lede: A visual journey through our survey, section by section. Every optimizer in it turns the same gradient into a different step: a scalar step size, a memory of past gradients, a per-coordinate scale, a curvature matrix, a Fisher metric, or a matrix norm. The guide builds the math from first principles, then walks through each family and asks the survey's question every time: *what information does it use, what geometry does it impose, and what does it cost?* Every visual is explained: what the axes are, what moves, and what to notice. Every surface is a real function; every ball runs a real optimizer.

parts.title: Introduction
parts.blurb: Why one gradient leaves so many decisions open, the two research questions, and the map of the survey.

parts.title: Mathematical preliminaries
parts.blurb: Taylor models, smoothness and safe steps, conditioning and rotated valleys, minibatch noise, and the variable-metric model that connects most of the survey. Appendix derivations are folded in where they belong.

parts.title: First-order optimization: from gradients to adaptivity (RQ1)
parts.blurb: GD and SGD, momentum, AdaGrad, RMSProp, Adam, AdamW, and the memory-light designs Adafactor and Lion.

parts.title: Second-order optimization: what curvature adds (RQ2)
parts.blurb: Newton's method and its safeguards, quasi-Newton and Hessian-free methods, and the difference between the Hessian, the Gauss-Newton matrix and the Fisher.

parts.title: Structured curvature and matrix-aware methods (RQ2)
parts.blurb: K-FAC, Shampoo, diagonal curvature (AdaHessian, Apollo, Sophia), SOAP, and Muon: what each one inverts, estimates or normalizes.

parts.title: Critical comparison
parts.blurb: Comparing the mathematics rather than the names: memory, cost, guarantees, stability, and a reproducible protocol, with a real measured dashboard.

parts.title: Open problems and conclusion
parts.blurb: Where the evidence runs out, and the survey's answers to RQ1 and RQ2.
